correctness.rationale: On complex l2(N0) with C_ij=1/(i+1) for j<=i and S e_j=e_(j+1), direct subtraction gives K_ij=-1/[i(i+1)] exactly for i>=1, j<i, zero otherwise. A=-K is Hilbert-Schmidt because sum_{i>=1} i/[i^2(i+1)^2]<infinity. For an h-by-h inclusive all-ones lower triangle L_h, the inverse first-difference Gram matrix has eigenvalues 4sin^2((2j-1)pi/(4h+2)), hence the exact displayed singular-value formula. I independently checked that formula by SVD for h=2,5,9 to <1e-15 absolute error. For p in (1/2,1), a dyadic row interval of size about 2^k J contributes a weighted strict triangle of S_p^p <=c_p(2^k J)^(1-2p) and, from earlier columns, a rank-one block of S_p^p <=c_p(2^k J)^(-p); summing gives ||P_[J,infty) A P_[J,infty)||_p^p <=C_p J^(1-2p). The columns before J add only rank one. This yields a uniform high-row counting error O(t^(-p)J^(1-2p)). Low rows have rank <=epsilon t^(-1/2)+1. On [epsilon/sqrt(t),M/sqrt(t)), finitely many geometric blocks have off-diagonal rank bounded independently of t, and diagonal singular counts bounded between constant-weight triangular spectra. The density is F(x)=(2/pi)arcsin(min(1,1/(2x^2))). The order of limits t->0, block ratio->1, epsilon->0 and M->infty is justified by the rank and Schatten tail estimates. F is integrable (tail O(x^-2)); Tonelli gives sqrt(t)N_A(t)->(2/pi)int_0^(pi/2)(2sin theta)^(-1/2)dtheta =Gamma(1/4)/(sqrt(2pi)Gamma(3/4))=A*. Monotone counting inversion yields n^2 s_n(K)->A*^2=Gamma(1/4)^2/[2pi Gamma(3/4)^2]. Then s_n(|K|^(1/2))~A*/n, so ordinary logarithmic means converge to A* and every normalized Dixmier trace has that value. Numerical beta evaluation gives A*=1.1803405990160964 and A*^2=1.3932039296856773. Independent exact-row-model finite SVDs on 200/400/512-square truncations and counting diagnostics are consistent but are not used as proof of the infinite limit.
residual_risks: The asymptotic is a hand-checked infinite-dimensional argument, not a Lean or external expert attestation.
Finite truncation singular values converge slowly and cannot by themselves establish the claimed coefficient; their comparisons are diagnostics only.
No general weighted-terraced or arbitrary Toeplitz-commutator singular law has been established by this package.

evidence: Bellavita–Stylogiannis Theorem 1.2 and 10.1 give modulo-S2 Mellin product identities and Toeplitz commutator ideal/essential spectral statements, not an s_n~constant*n^-2 law.
The 1996 Volterra theorem concerns L2(0,1) kernels x^-beta(x-t)^(alpha-1), and specifies a general order and unweighted fractional integral constant, not this discrete matrix coefficient.
Pushnitski studies absolutely continuous spectrum and spectral density for Hardy kernel matrices, as opposed to the compact strict triangular operator here.
The sharp trace-class endpoint for monotone-modulus Rhaly matrices is a membership criterion sum |eta_n|log(n+2)<infty, not this n^-2 singular-value coefficient.

originality.rationale: The exact leading n^(-2) singular coefficient and resulting measurable square-root modulus Dixmier trace for the specific discrete CS-SC were not determined by the accessed stronger-looking results. The same-operator earlier two-sided bounds asserted in the source would not imply convergence, even if their priority is confirmed. The newest full primary text read establishes Mellin/Toeplitz and S2 commutator conclusions, not this sharper pointwise limit. Published neighboring coefficients concern n^(-1) generalized C_t; a continuous Hardy-Volterra commutator has a different kernel. Best-of-knowledge PASS, explicitly limited by unread original Sang/Rhaly and potentially dominating general discrete Weyl asymptotics.
residual_risks: A general pre-existing discrete Hardy/terraced-matrix Weyl law or Birman–Solomyak-style theorem might imply the entire result by nontrivial reduction, even if the exact gamma constant is not indexed by name.

value.rationale: The commutator of two canonical bounded operators is a natural compact operator, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Exact n^2*s_n fixes the leading cost of optimal rank-n approximation unavailable from mere compactness, Schatten membership or c n^-2<=s_n<=C n^-2. The associated unique Dixmier trace of |CS-SC|^(1/2) identifies a noncommutative residue at a sharp critical ideal exponent, of independent value for operator-ideal and Toeplitz commutator questions. The analytic multiscale counting proof is not a textbook renaming or a finite known-table computation. The specific coefficient can be used directly in sharp numerical approximation and spectral regularity questions, without claiming an entire new theory of all weighted matrices.
residual_risks: No downstream generalization or unrelated application is claimed; the value rests on the exact natural operator invariant itself.
If an existing general Weyl theorem already yields the coefficient, both originality and contribution assessment would require reevaluation.

final_claim: For K=CS-SC on complex l2(N0), with C the classical discrete Cesàro matrix and S the forward unilateral shift, lim_(n->infty) n^2 s_n(K) = Gamma(1/4)^2/(2 pi Gamma(3/4)^2).
